title: MCP Tool Registry v1.0
description: Schema for the per-project MCP tool registry — a single inventory of every MCP server declared in .mcp.json and every tool that server exposes. Acceptance criterion §34 row 10: `claude mcp list` output MUST match this registry (exit 1 on drift). Distinct from the mapping files: gsc-tool-mapping.json / dataforseo-endpoint-mapping.json / scrapling-output-mapping.json describe HOW a tool feeds Excel sheets; this registry describes WHICH tools are declared to exist and their version locks + capabilities + auth method. Keeps the runtime surface (what Claude can actually call) auditable against the configured surface (what the project said it runs). Version locks here use the same exact-pin pattern as S3-D-1 (e.g. dataforseo-mcp-server); the authoritative value lives in servers.dataforseo.version_lock and is asserted equal to the @<ver> pinned in .mcp.json by tests/schemas/test_mcp_registry_versions_match_mcp_json.py (P0-03) — do not hardcode the number here.

generated_at.description: Last time the registry was reconciled against `claude mcp list`. Older-than-SLA → AMBER in consistency-report.schema_validation.

reconcile_sla_hours.description: Acceptable staleness before consistency check warns. Weekly is the default operational cadence.

servers.description: Keys are MCP server short names — the same keys used in .mcp.json mcpServers. Closed to the known 4 + project-local servers for audit clarity.

unmapped_tools_policy.description: What to do when `claude mcp list` returns a tool not listed in servers[].tools — strict fails audit, permissive records it with a warning.

external_user_dependencies.description: Tool surfaces a skill needs that this plugin does NOT install — they must already exist in the operator's own MCP client (user-level). Kept OUT of `servers` (and .mcp.json) on purpose so the F-24 .mcp.json↔registry server-key invariant is not tripped (P1-13). Keys are the external server short-name (e.g. higgsfield).

externalUserDependency.description: A user-level external MCP dependency (P1-13). Deliberately NOT a `servers` entry / .mcp.json server, so F-24 (.mcp.json↔registry server-key sync) stays honest.

transport.description: user_external = configured per-user in the operator's MCP client, not installed by this plugin.

not_in_mcp_json.description: True asserts this dependency is intentionally absent from .mcp.json (keeps the F-24 invariant honest).

tools.description: Unprefixed tool names the skills call (e.g. generate_image → mcp__higgsfield__generate_image at runtime).

required_by_skills.description: Skill names (skills/**/SKILL.md `name`) that declare these tools in mcp_tools.

serverName.description: Canonical short server name. gsc + dataforseo + scrapling + sf are the four external feeds (sf added v1.8 Phase 1 D-SF-02 for Screaming Frog 24 native MCP, HTTP transport); platinum_seo_core is the plugin's own server; project_local is the escape hatch for per-project-only servers. adstark is the local CRM / task-board server used by refresh-audit; xquik is the remote API proxy reached over mcp-remote and its tool inventory is reconstructed from observed calls, not read from the server.

authMethod.description: How credentials are sourced. keychain = macOS keychain via keychain_helpers.py (preferred, §30); env_var = process env (CI/CD); user_config = ~/.config/seo-core/secrets (fallback); none = tool exposes no sensitive endpoints.

runtime.description: How the server is launched. npx spawns a Node package; python spawns a Python package; stdio is the built-in plugin server (no spawn); http is a remote-hosted MCP endpoint.

mcp_json_key.description: Explicit alias for the matching key in .mcp.json mcpServers when it differs from this registry's canonical (lowercase) server key — e.g. scrapling here is 'ScraplingServer' in .mcp.json (D-SF-02). Mirrors validate_invariants._MCP_JSON_KEY_ALIASES; the F-24 invariant + tests/schemas/test_skill_mcp_tools_exist_in_registry.py rely on it. Omit when the .mcp.json key already equals the registry key.

package.description: npm package or pypi package id. Required for runtime=npx or runtime=python.

version_lock.description: Exact version string the project locks to (no semver ranges for MCP servers — drift is a silent failure surface per §13.1). Use 'none' for runtime=stdio (built-in, versioned by the plugin).

endpoint_url.description: Only for runtime=http. Captured so rotation/drift audits know where to look.

auth_config.description: Non-secret auth config — key names only, never values.

keychain_service.description: macOS keychain service name (seo-core-gsc, seo-core-dfs, etc.).

env_vars.description: Env var NAMES expected at runtime (e.g. DATAFORSEO_USERNAME). Values never stored.

user_config_keys.description: user_config keys referenced via ${user_config.X} interpolation in .mcp.json.

capabilities.description: High-level capability tags, for budget/policy routing. e.g. 'paid' → governed by budget_policy; 'write' → needs PreToolUse confirmation; 'read' → no side effects.

rate_limit.description: Free text; e.g. '200 queries per 100 seconds' (GSC), '30 qps account' (DFS SERP).

tools.description: Every callable tool this server exposes (subset of `claude mcp list` output for this server). Registry MUST be complete for servers with unmapped_tools_policy=strict.

tool_name.description: Fully qualified short name (gsc__search_analytics, dataforseo__serp_organic_live_advanced, scrapling__stealthy_fetch). Claude Code runtime surfaces this as mcp__{server}__{tool}; this registry stores the unprefixed form used in mapping files.

category.description: Coarse bucket for routing + budget. Mirrors the dataforseo endpoint_groups + gsc use-case families.

used_by_mappings.description: Which mapping files reference this tool. Lint: union of these refs must cover every tool listed here (zero-orphan tool contract).

cost_credits_per_call.description: DFS-style credit cost. 0 for free/GSC. Absent for scrapling_local (no per-call cost metric — measured in runtime cost instead).

cache_ttl_hours.description: Default cache TTL. Per-use-case overrides live in the mapping files.

deprecated.description: True when the upstream MCP server has deprecated this tool but our version_lock still supports it. Emits AMBER until we bump the version lock.
